newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE ON FRIDAY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE ON FRIDAY.

text.p: Short term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted unchanged from Thursday's levels in early Friday trade but dealers said they might go up in the day as most players hunted around for scarce money.

"The market is rather short at the moment. Rates haven't moved yet but they might edge up later because everyone will be looking around for money to square off their positions at settlement," one dealer said.
Meanwhile on Friday morning, discount houses were purchasing 91-day treasury bills from the central bank at 19 percent and re-selling them in the market at 18.75 percent.

Negotiable certificates of deposit with maturity of 30, 60 and 90 days were indicated at 21 percent (buying) and 19.25 percent (selling), unchanged from Thursday, as were bankers acceptance bills at 19.50 and 19 percent. Call money also held steady at 19 percent.
